Plan the BLAST search strategy

Source: R/blast_strategy.R
blast_strategy.Rd

Decide how parallel_blast() splits a search: how many blastn processes run at once, how many threads each one uses, the BLAST+ multithreading mode and how many query sequences go in each batch.

Each blastn process reads the whole database once per batch, so the cost of a search grows with the number of batches and of concurrent processes, not with the number of sequences. The rules below come from the BLASTr benchmark (dev/benchmark/ in the source repository):

  • Small databases (under small_db_gb): reading the database is cheap. One single-threaded process per core, each with an equal share of the sequences; results are identical to one search per sequence.

  • Large databases that fit in RAM: few processes with many threads each, splitting the database between the threads (mt_mode = 2). Threads per process are limited to the number of database volumes and to max_threads (32); the remaining cores run more processes, each with its own share of the sequences. On core_nt (92 volumes), with 32 cores one blastn searched 500 sequences in 170 s, against 164 s for 2 processes x 16 threads and 243 s for 8 x 4 (2000 sequences: 239 s, 311 s, 367 s). With 64 cores, one blastn with 64 threads was slower than with 32 (152 s vs 120 s for 500 sequences, 265 s vs 206 s for 2000), while 2 processes x 32 threads took 87 s and 182 s.

  • Large databases that do not fit in RAM: one process and one batch, so the database is read from disk only once (on core_nt, each extra read cost about 6 minutes). The ETA is then unknown until the end.

Otherwise, batches are kept at or under max_batch_size sequences and there is at least one batch per process. Each batch reads the whole database again (about 70 s on core_nt in RAM, with 32 threads; 2000 sequences in 80 batches took 1190 s instead of 345 s in 4), so batches are only as many as needed for the ETA to show up during long searches.

Usage

blast_strategy(
  n_seqs,
  db_path,
  total_cores = 1L,
  ram_gb = NULL,
  num_threads = NULL,
  batch_size = NULL,
  mt_mode = NULL,
  small_db_gb = 1,
  max_batch_size = 1000L,
  max_threads = 32L
)

Arguments

n_seqs

Number of unique query sequences.

db_path

Path(s) to the BLAST database(s). Several databases are searched together; their sizes are added.

total_cores

Number of CPU cores (threads) to use in total.

ram_gb

RAM available for the search, in GB. NULL uses the total RAM of the machine.

num_threads, batch_size, mt_mode

Optional fixed values; NULL chooses automatically.

small_db_gb

Size under which a database is treated as small.

max_batch_size

Largest number of sequences in a single batch.

max_threads

Largest number of threads for one blastn process on a large database; more threads than this did not make BLAST faster.

Value

A list of class blastr_strategy with processes, threads, mt_mode, batch_size, n_batches, the database facts (db_path, db_gb, db_volumes, ram_gb, fits_ram) and reason.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
blast_strategy(
  n_seqs = 2000,
  db_path = "/data/databases/core_nt/core_nt",
  total_cores = 32,
  ram_gb = 256
)
} # }
